title: Predictive Cohort Quarantine and Handshake for Shadow-to-Canary Transitions
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduces a Predictive Cohort Quarantine subsystem and a deterministic handshake protocol for transitioning traffic from shadow to canary. Backwards-compatible with existing rollout CRDs; provides metrics-quorum gating and post-rollout audit playback support.
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently see noisy early canaries where transient spikes in error rates (from outlier cohorts) cause safe rollbacks but produce a lot of manual churn. This PR implements a deterministic handshake plus a short predictive quarantine stage to reduce flapping: a shadow cohort that shows anomalous signals is temporarily quarantined and then handshaken into a canary only when cohort-level drift confidence and metric-quorum criteria are met.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a predictive quarantine controller that watches cohort-level metrics (latency histogram tails, token-level error rates, classifier drift score) and applies a short quarantine TTL with exponential backoff on re-admission attempts. 2) Implements a handshake protocol between the shadow router and the canary admission controller to ensure session affinity and KV cache warmup are respected during handoff. 3) Adds a new 'quarantine' state to the rollout CRD and migration code that keeps historical traces for audit playback and replay-based regression simulation. 4) Ships e2e tests and a small local simulator for teams to validate policy tunings before enabling on Dedicated clusters.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear: ENG-7832) - [x] Rollout CRD extension schema + migration - [x] Handshake protocol and session-affinity preservation - [x] Predictive quarantine TTL + backoff policy - [x] Metrics-quorum gates wired to console dashboards - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Canary e2e playback simulator - [x] Updated docs and upgrade notes

Risk and mitigation: The new quarantine state is additive and optional; existing rollouts default to current behavior. We've throttled the default re-admission rate and set conservative thresholds. Migration path: controllers will annotate legacy rollouts and gradually enable 'predictive-quarantine' via a feature flag.

Related work: RFC in ENG-7899, follow-ups expected to integrate with model-quality eval sets (future) and to expose policy knobs in Redwood Console.

Merging notes: CI passed after two flaky test reruns; manual canary on staging ran for 48h with stable metrics before merge.
